items.canonicalSource: The child node's own header is canonical for its depth status, and each sub-domain index's children table is canonical for that sub-domain's hypothesis count (each count verified against the leaf files' own unique DT-NN ids). Specifically: 10.06-live-setlist-pro-reporting.md:5 '> **Status**: [PARTIAL]'; 10.09-distribution-calendar-money-in-flight.md:5 '> **Status**: [PARTIAL]'; 10.02-statement-ingestion-normalization/10.02-statement-ingestion-normalization-index.md:20-24 (17+13+13+10+15 = 68); 10.03-calculation-recoupment/10.03-calculation-recoupment-index.md:20-23 (13+13+3+3 = 32); 10.05-recovery-leakage/10.05-recovery-leakage-index.md:20-22 (12+3+3 = 18).
items.summary: Confirmed and fixed. The domain index was the only drifted location — every sub-domain index and every leaf file was already internally consistent, and I re-derived all five sub-domain hypothesis totals from the leaves' own unique DT-NN ids rather than trusting the sub-indexes. Five stale values swept in the Children table plus the classification note re-scoped: 10.06 and 10.09 status [SURFACE] -> [PARTIAL] (their files declare [PARTIAL], last updated 2026-07-17, one day after the index was written); 10.02 15 -> 68 hypotheses, 10.03 12 -> 32, 10.05 9 -> 18 (10.01's 19 and 10.04's 11 were already correct — those two sub-domains never deepened, which is exactly why they did not drift). The 'All [SURFACE].' assertion and the '81 Deep Think hypotheses logged' figure were not wrong, they were unlabelled: 19+15+12+11+9+15 = 81 is precisely the classification-pass total on 2026-07-16, so the note is a frozen record that had been read as a present-tense claim. Re-scoped it as a record of that pass, added the current total (148 across the sub-domains + 15 across 10.06-10.10 = 163), and stated the precedence rule the tree already operates by — the child's own '> **Status**:' header declares its depth, the index only restates it. That last clause is what kills the forced invention: a downstream stage now has a stated rule for which side wins instead of two silent contradictions. Also bumped the index's Last updated to 2026-07-30. Children table verified at 6 columns / 7 pipes across all 12 rows after editing; no canonical file touched.

crossDomainNotes: 02-credits-attribution/credits-attribution-index.md carries the identical defect pattern and was not in my shard: its classification note asserts 'All `[SURFACE]`.' while the table immediately below lists 02.06 Credit Role & Instrument Taxonomy as `[DEEP]` with 14 hypotheses. Same root cause — a frozen classification-pass note read as a live claim. Whoever owns domain 02 should apply the same re-scoping. This also confirms the fix I made follows tree convention rather than inventing one: sibling domain indexes do update their Status/Deep Think columns as children deepen (02.06 is current), while the prose note stays at its classification-pass wording.

The general shape — domain-index child metadata going stale after a deepening pass that only touched the child and its immediate parent index — is likely present in every domain that has been partially deepened. It is a sweep problem, not a per-domain judgement, and would be better prevented by generating the Status and Deep Think columns from the child headers than by re-auditing them each round.
